annotatedSteps.description: Placing solutions P and Q on the pH scale
annotatedSteps.studentWork: P will be at pH 13 and Q will be at pH 1.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Solution P is a strong acid and should be placed at pH 0–2, while Q is a strong base and should be placed at pH 12–14.
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Solution P (strong acid) is placed at pH 0–2 (or ~1) and solution Q (strong base) is placed at pH 12–14 (or ~13).

annotatedSteps.description: Naming compounds to increase and decrease pH of neutral solution
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
(i) To increase pH - add sodium hydroxide.
(ii) To decrease pH - add hydrochloric acid.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly identified a base (NaOH) to increase pH and an acid (HCl) to decrease pH.

annotatedSteps.description: Effect on hydronium ion concentration when pH decreases from 4 to 2
annotatedSteps.studentWork: When pH decreases from 4 to 2, the hydronium ion (H3O+) concentration increases.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly stated that hydronium ion concentration increases.

annotatedSteps.description: Colour change shown by pH paper when pH decreases from 4 to 2
annotatedSteps.studentWork: The pH paper colour changes from orange to red.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct colour transition from orange to red identified.

teacherNote: Well done on parts (b) and (c) for accurately identifying compounds and interpreting pH changes on hydronium ion concentration and indicator colors. Be careful with the pH scale: acids have pH values below 7 (strong acids near 0–1), while bases have pH values above 7 (strong bases near 13–14).

rubric.point: Placement of solution P (strong acid, pH ~0–2) and solution Q (strong base, pH ~12–14) on the pH scale
Naming a suitable compound to (i) increase pH (base/alkali) and (ii) decrease pH (acid)
Effect of decreasing pH from 4 to 2 on hydronium ion concentration (increases)
